title: Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour
institution: socius labs, London; London School of Economics and Political Science (affiliations as printed)
description: Paper that fine-tunes fourteen base language models from 135M to 14B parameters (Qwen3-Base, Llama-3, SmolLM2 and SmolLM3, OLMo-2 and OLMo-3) with rank-stabilised LoRA on Psych-101, using Centaur's train-test splits and prompt templates without modification, and compares them with a reproduced Centaur-70B. It reports that in-distribution (held-out participants) 'scale barely matters' and '0.6B to 1B parameters suffice to match a 70B baseline', while on the eighteen held-out experiments of Psych-201-RT larger models generalise better. Diagnostics strip four prompt channels (task instructions, stimuli, outcome feedback, choice history) across 27 experiments and permute trial order. The authors propose such models as noise-ceiling estimators whose 'scope remains bounded by the paradigms seen in training'.

Methods (p. 3): Psych-101 with Centaur's splits and templates; six task types; fourteen base models; supervised fine-tuning with loss masked to human response tokens; rank-stabilised LoRA on all linear layers, one epoch, AdamW at 5e-5, bf16, one A100 80GB GPU
results: on Psych-101 eight matched models span 0.509 to 0.537 nats, a band containing the Centaur-70B reproduction; on Psych-201-RT (18 held-out experiments) they span 0.788 to 1.033

diagnostics: instruction-ablated, content-masked and history-only conditions; masking stimulus and feedback content 'destroys 75.7% of learned information'; 50 random trial-order permutations, THINGS odd-one-out versus intertemporal choice
Reproducibility Statement (p. 11): code at github.com/socius-org/Centauri, LoRA adapters on Hugging Face, Psych-101 from Binz et al. (2025) with the same splits and templates
PDF: 87 pages; printed page numbers equal physical index + 1
